title: Calibration artifact provenance, audit-friendly hashing, and reversible rollouts for quant profiles
creator: Ava Mitchell
description:
Goal: Make FP8/INT8 quantization artifacts fully reproducible, cryptographically auditable, and safe to roll back in production. Deliver an artifact manifest schema, deterministic calibration workflow requirements, a hashing+signature strategy for provenance, CI gating rules, and a rollback/playback plan for model serving routes.

Problem statement:
- Calibration outputs (scale/zero-point, per-channel params, clipping thresholds) have been difficult to reproduce across runs because of non-deterministic batch ordering, RNG seeds, and toolchain drift.
- Lack of a canonical artifact manifest and signature makes it hard to audit which calibration produced a given profile and to verify that a profile served in production corresponds to a validated calibration run.
- Rollback currently relies on ad-hoc S3 objects; we need safer, auditable reversible rollouts with automatic validation gates.

Proposed solution (summary):
1) Artifact manifest: a small JSON that contains: artifact_id (UUID), profile_version (semver), model_checkpoint_sha256, tokenizer_sha256, calibration_dataset_id, calibration_dataset_sha256, calibration_seed, calibration_order_hash, calibration_toolchain_git_commit, quant_parameters (bits, per-channel, symmetric/affine flags), runtime_target (runtime-1.22), creation_timestamp, signer_key_id, signature. Store manifest alongside binary profile in artifact-registry.

2) Hashing strategy: canonicalize manifest fields (sorted keys, stable serialization), then compute sha256(manifest_without_signature). This becomes artifact_checksum. Include both artifact_checksum and signature=KMS.sign(artifact_checksum) in manifest. The signature is required for promotion to production.

3) Deterministic calibration workflow rules: fixed RNG seeds, fixed batch order (pre-shuffle once and store order hash), fixed floating point rounding mode, pinned numpy/torch/quant libs versions (toolchain_git_commit required). Documented calibration harness entrypoints must be used by CI (no ad-hoc scripts).

4) Validation & gating: every candidate quant profile must run the canonical evaluation suite (eval bundle) with pre-registered prompts and metrics (accuracy delta, perplexity, token-level MRR). Gate thresholds: accuracy_drop <= 0.5% absolute OR relative quality degradation <= 2% for top-1 tasks (configurable per model). If thresholds breached -> automatic block and alert on Slack + ticket.

5) Rollout & rollback: artifact registry retains last N (configurable, default 10) signed profiles per model-version. Rollout uses canary traffic split (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated metric checks at each stage. A rollback action consists of re-promoting the previous signed artifact and re-running the gating validation. Rollbacks must be immutable operations recorded in audit logs with who/when/why.

6) Registry layout & naming: s3://redwood-quant-artifacts/{model_name}/{model_ckpt_sha256}/{profile_semver}/{artifact_uuid}/{profile.bin,manifest.json,validation_report.json}. Include lifecycle policy: cold archive after 180 days, retain minimum 10 snapshots for 365 days.

7) CI integration: PR pipeline must generate candidate artifacts (with manifest), run deterministic calibration, run eval suite, and attach validation_report.json to the PR. Promotion to 'production' tag requires a signed manifest and an approver (owner of model component).

Acceptance criteria (must be testable):
- A reproducible calibration run that, when re-run with manifest inputs, produces the same artifact_checksum.
- A CI flow that refuses to promote unsiged or mismatched manifests.
- Rollout process that can revert to the previous signed artifact within 5 minutes and records the event in audit logs.
- E2E test demonstrating rollback from promoted FP8 artifact to previous INT8 artifact for a small test-model.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Signature scheme: prefer KMS-signed ECDSA for auditability; evaluate HSM latency for high-frequency promotions.
- How many fields to include in canonicalization vs. computed metadata (we should avoid including ephemeral metrics in checksum).
- Backward compatibility with existing unversioned profiles (migration script required).

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: finalize manifest schema, hashing + signature design, and deterministic calibration checklist.
- Week 2: instrument calibration harness to emit manifest and canonicalized serialization; add KMS sign/verify helpers.
- Week 3: CI pipeline update to run eval suite and attach validation reports; initial PR flow.
- Week 4: implement artifact registry layout, retention policy, and basic rollback API + console hooks.
- Week 5: run migration of 2 sample models and validate E2E rollback.

Notes for reviewers:
- See attached sample manifest (s3 path above) for exact field names and types.
- This is intentionally conservative: we prefer reproducible but slightly more verbose manifests to speed audits and incident debugging.
